text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Around 350,000 new passenger cars were sold in Poland in the first 11 months of this year, which represents Europe's highest growth rate of 39 percent, the Samar monitoring agency representative Wojciech Drzewiecki said.
- The Daewoo FSO automaker's director Jin Chul Suk will return to Warsaw to resume his post following a trial in Seoul, the plant's spokeswoman Krystyna Danilczyk said.
- Poland's transport minister Boguslaw Liberadzki has repeated his intention to include the road tax in the fuel price, a move previously blocked by the finance minstry which feared inflation.

- The following banks will act as money market dealers next year: Bank Gdanski, Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG), Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS), Pekao SA, Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH), Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE), Bank Slaski (BSK), Citibank Poland, ING Bank Warsaw, Kredyt Bank, Polski Bank Investycyjny (PBI), PKO BP, Raiffeisen Centrobank, Societe Generale and Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK), the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank said.

- The city of Warsaw will not issue municipal bonds next year, Warsaw's president Marcin Swiecicki said. An issue may take place a year later to fund a new bridge in south Warsaw. The city had planned to issue bonds worth 300 million zlotys.
- Lodz-based Petrobank has called an extraordinary shareholders' meeting which is expected to change the bank's name to LG Petrobank SA and replace its current board, the management said.

- The major state-owned PZU insurance firm will increase the price rates of compulsory motor liability insurance by 33 percent on average, which is 10 points less than the rate indcrease published last week, the management said.
NOWA EUROPA

- Bank Gdanski decided to organise a banking consortium to provide a $100 million credit for construction of five ships by the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard. The ships will be contracted by Germany's Scholler and building will start in February 1996.
- The Szczecin shipyard will deliver 21 ships to contractors in 1997 and launch 22 vessels. The ships were ordered by shipowners from Germany, Cyprus, Greece, Australia, Hongkong and Africa.
- A new yacht port is under construction in Leba, northern Poland. The facility will cost 3.5 million zlotys and it is financed from the EU's PHARE and Crossborder funds.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The first nine km strip of the Swiecie bypass linking the city of Bydgoszcz with the A-1 motorway now under construction was opened yesterday. The strip cost 73 million zlotys to build while the bypass will cost 103 million zlotys, the transport ministry said.
- Walbrzych province governor Henryk Golebiowski has held talks with Germany's Volkswagen automaker on its future investment plans in the province's special economic zone.

- Polish banks Pekao SA, BPH, PKO BP, PBG, and BSK provided credits for car purchases worth around 1.5 billion zlotys in 1996, the CASE socio-economic analysis centre researcher Andrzej Bratkowski said.
ZYCIE - The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has permitted the new Atut trust fund to start operations by the end of the first quarter of 1997, KPW said.
- The first stage of modernisation of the Bobrowniki commodity transit border pass on the Polish-Belarus border has been completed. Construction work cost 20 million zlotys.
PARKIET - The listed Budimex construction firm has received 87 contracts in Germany worth 136.8 milllion zlotys, Budimex said.
- The listed Forte furniture maker has received a five million marks credit from ING Warsaw bank to repay credits and loans drawn in the past.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
